newsitem.title: INDIA: Supply hold-ups, buying underpin Indian castorseed.
newsitem.headline: Supply hold-ups, buying underpin Indian castorseed.

text.p: Indian castorseed for September delivery rose to 1,151/1,152 rupees per quintal on Thursday from 1,147 the day before on the back of speculative buying, traders said.
They said the buying had been triggered by fresh overseas enquiries and limited arrivals from producing centres due to widespread rains.
For Indian castoroil, foreign buyers were bidding at 715-720 dollars per tonne.

Groundnut oil held steady at 372/373 rupees per 10 kg amid arrivals of 40-50 tonnes compared with an average of 80-100 tonnes, though demand was subdued. In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil was quiet at 595 rupees per 15 kg.
In Bombay imported palm-oil remained steady at 251/252 rupees per 10 kg on outstation enquiries and limited offerings by local importers due to low prices.
"Local prices are now lower against our import cost and if we sell, we will invite losses at this level," said one importer said.
